x: It means by the Almighty’s saying to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, meaning: Indeed, We have decreed for you, O Muhammad, a judgment for whoever hears it or hears it, over those of the disbelievers of your people who oppose you and are hostile to you, and We have decreed for you victory and triumph over them, so that you may thank your Lord and praise Him for His blessing in His decreeing for you over them and His granting you what He granted you, and that you may glorify Him and seek His forgiveness, so that your Lord may forgive you for your deeds, whatever sin you committed before He granted you what He granted you, and whatever sins you committed after He granted you what He granted you. That is what you thanked Him for and sought His forgiveness. We have chosen this statement in interpreting this verse because of the evidence of the statement of God, the Exalted, the Majestic,
h

When there comes the help of God and the conquest, and you see the people entering into the religion of God in multitudes, then exalt [God] with praise of your Lord and ask His forgiveness. Indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance

, as God, the Exalted, commanded him to exalt with praise of his Lord when God’s help and the conquest of Mecca came to him, and to ask His forgiveness, and informed him that He is the Accepter of repentance for whoever does that.
In that is a clear statement that the statement of God, the Exalted, the Majestic,
h
So that God may forgive you what is past of your sin and what is to come

is only information from God, the Exalted, to His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, about His reward for his thanks to Him, for the blessing that He bestowed upon him by revealing to him what He conquered, because God, the Exalted, rewards His servants for their deeds and nothing else. And after that, in the authenticity of the report about him, may God bless him and grant him peace, “that he would stand until his feet swelled, so it was said to him: O Messenger of God, do you do this while your past and future sins have been forgiven? He said: Should I not be a grateful servant?” This is clear evidence that what we have said is the correct statement, and that God, the Blessed and Exalted, only promised His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, forgiveness for his past sins, the opening that He opened for him, and the coming ones, based on his gratitude to Him, for the blessings that He bestowed upon him.

Likewise, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would say: I seek forgiveness from God and repent to Him for every hundred times. If the statement in this regard was that God the Most High informed His Prophet that He had forgiven him for his past and future sins in a manner other than the one we have mentioned, then His command to him to seek forgiveness after this verse, and the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) seeking forgiveness from his Lord for his sins after it, would not have had a rational meaning. For seeking forgiveness means: the servant asking his Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, to forgive his sins. So if there are no sins that can be forgiven, then his asking Him to forgive them would have no meaning, because it is impossible for him to say: O God, forgive me for a sin that I did not commit.

Some of them interpreted this to mean: So that He may forgive you for your past sins before the message, and for those that came after until the time when He said: Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest * That God may forgive you what is past of your sin and what is to come. As for the conquest that God Almighty promised His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, this number in gratitude to him for it, it is what was mentioned in the truce that took place between the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the polytheists of Quraysh at Al-Hudaybiyah. It was mentioned that this Surah was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, upon his return from Al-Hudaybiyah after the truce that took place between him and his people. And similar to what we said about the meaning of His statement, Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest. Conquest means judgment. Mention the narration of the one who said that this Surah was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at the time mentioned.

c: Humaid bin Masada told us: Bishr bin al-Mufaddal told us: Dawud told us on the authority of Amer:
m: Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest. He said: Al-Hudaybiyyah.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, he said: He slaughtered him at Al-Hudaibiyah and shaved Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest. his head. Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Buzayʿ narrated: Abu Bahr narrated: Shuʿbah narrated: Jamiʿ ibn Shaddad narrated: ʿAbdur-Rahman ibn Abi ʿUlqamah said: I heard ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud say: “When we returned from Al-Hudaybiyyah, we camped and slept, and we did not wake up until the sun had risen. We woke up and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was asleep. We said: ‘Wake him up.’ The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) woke up and said: ‘Do as you used to do, for the same applies to one who sleeps or forgets.’ We missed the she-camel of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and found its halter caught in a tree. I brought it to him and he mounted it. While we were traveling, the revelation came to him. When it came to him, he would be distressed, but when he recovered, he informed us that the following had been revealed to him: ‘Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest.’”

c: Ahmad ibn al-Muqaddam narrated to us: Al-Mu'tamir narrated to us:
m: I heard my father narrating on the authority of Qatada on the authority of Anas ibn Malik who said: “When we returned from the Battle of Hudaybiyyah, we were prevented from performing our rituals. We were in a state of sadness and depression. Then God, the Almighty, revealed: ‘Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, that God may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what will follow and complete His favor upon you and guide you to a straight path,’ or as God willed. Then the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘A verse has been revealed to me that is more beloved to me than the entire world.’”

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Urooba, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas bin Malik,
m: regarding the verse, Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, he said: It was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on his return from Hudaybiyyah, and they had been prevented from performing their rituals. He had slaughtered the sacrificial animals at Hudaybiyyah, and his companions were feeling depressed and sad with him. He said, A verse has been revealed to me that is dearer to me than the entire world. So he recited, Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, * That God may forgive you what is past of your sin and what is to come ... to His saying, exalted. His companions said, Congratulations, O Messenger of God! God has made clear to us what He will do with you, so what will He do with us? So God revealed this verse after it, That He may admit the believing men and believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein eternally ... to His saying, And that is, in the sight of God, a great attainment.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told me: Abu Dawud told us: Ibn Hammam told us: Qatada told us on the authority of Anas:
m: This verse was revealed, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas,
m: in a similar manner, except that he said in his hadith: “A man from the people said: ‘Congratulations to you, O Messenger of God.’ He also said: ‘So God explained what He would do to His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and what He would do to them.’”

c: Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: "The verse, 'That God may forgive you your sins, past and future,' was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he was returning from al-Hudaybiyyah. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, 'A verse has been revealed to me that is dearer to me than anything on the earth.' Then he recited it to them, and they said, 'Congratulations and good report, O Prophet of God. God, the Exalted, has explained to you what He did to you, so what will He do with us?' Then the verse, 'That He may admit the believing men and believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow' was revealed to him... until His saying, 'a great attainment.'"

c: Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of ʿIkrimah, who said:
m: When this verse was revealed, Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, that God may forgive you what is past of your sin and what is to come and complete His favor upon you and guide you to a straight path, they said, Congratulations and good report for you, O Messenger of God! So what is for us? Then the verse was revealed, That He may admit the believing men and believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein eternally, and remove from them their misdeeds. (al-Fath 48:5).

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us:
m: I heard Qatada narrating on the authority of Anas regarding this verse: Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest. He said: Al-Hudaybiyyah.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Yahya bin Hammad told us: Aba Awana told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, who said:
m: We did not consider the conquest of Mecca to be anything but the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah. Abu Kurayb narrated: Yaʿla ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, on the authority of ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Siyah, on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Thabit, on the authority of Abu Waʿil, who said: “Sahl ibn Hunayf spoke on the day of Siffin and said: ‘O people, accuse yourselves. You saw us on the day of Hudaybiyyah,’ meaning the peace treaty that was between the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the polytheists. If we had seen fighting, we would have fought. ʿUmar came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘O Messenger of God, are we not on the right path and they on the wrong path? Aren’t our dead in Paradise and their dead in Hell? ’ He said: ‘Yes. ’ He said: ‘Then why should we give up our religion and go back before God has judged between us and them? ’ He said: ‘O Ibn al-Khattab, I am the Messenger of God, and He will never let me down. ’ He said: ‘So he went back in anger, but he could not be patient until he went to Abu

evidence.text: Then he recited it to them, and they said, 'Congratulations and good report, O Prophet of God.

x: God Almighty says: That God may forgive you your sins, past and future, and complete His favor upon you, and guide you to a straight path.
God Almighty says: And God will grant you a mighty victory.
God the Most High means by His statement,
h
It is He who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers

, that God sent down tranquility and reassurance into the hearts of the believers in God and His Messenger, with faith and the truth with which God sent you, O Muhammad. The difference of opinion among the people of interpretation regarding the meaning of tranquility has already been mentioned before, and the correct view regarding this is based on evidence that makes it unnecessary to repeat it here. So that they may increase in faith along with their faith. He says: So that they may increase in their belief in the new obligations that God has imposed on them, which were not binding on them before. So that they may increase in faith along with their faith. He says: So that they may increase in their belief in the obligations that were binding on them before that. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali narrated to me, he said: Abu Saleh narrated to us, he said: Muawiyah narrated to me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement,
h
It is He who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers

, he said: Tranquility means mercy, that they might increase in faith along with their [present] faith, he said: Indeed, God, the Most High, sent to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, the testimony that there is no god but God. When they believed in it, He increased them in Hajj, then He perfected their religion for them, saying, This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you (5:3). Ibn Abbas said: So the most authentic, true, and perfect faith of the people of the earth and the people of the heavens is the testimony that there is no god but God. And His statement,
h
And to God belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth
, God Almighty says:
h
And to God belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth

, supporters by which He takes revenge on whomever He wills of His enemies. And God is All-Knowing, All-Wise, God Almighty says: And God has always had knowledge of what was to come before it came into being, and of what He created, and He is Wise in His management.

x: God Almighty says: Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, so that you may be grateful to your Lord and praise Him for that, and He will forgive you your past and future sins. And let the believers in God praise their Lord and thank Him for His favor upon them, for the conquest He granted them and decreed between them and their enemies among the polytheists, by making them victorious over them. Thus, He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever, and that He will expiate for them their evil deeds with the good deeds they do, as thanks from them to their Lord for what He decreed for them and bestowed upon them. And that is with God a great attainment. God Almighty says: And what God promised them of this promise, that is, their admission to gardens beneath which rivers flow, and His expiation of their evil deeds with the good deeds they do, is with God for them a great attainment.

He says: A triumph on their part for what they had hoped for and strove for, and salvation from what they had been fearing of a great punishment from God. It was previously mentioned that this verse was revealed when the believers said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or he recited to them the words of God Almighty: Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, that God may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what will follow. This is for you, O Messenger of God, so what is for us? It is a clarification from God to them of what He will do with them.

c: Ali told us: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
That He may admit the believing men and believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow
...to His statement, and remove from them their misdeeds. So God Almighty informed His Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. His saying,
h
That the believing men and women may enter is based on the lam of his saying

, That God may forgive you what came before of your sin, with the interpretation of repeating the statement, Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest * That God may forgive you, Indeed, We have granted you that the believing men and women may enter gardens beneath which rivers flow. For this reason, the waw that is entered into the statement for the purpose of conjunction was not used, so He did not say, And that the believing men and women may enter.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, that God may forgive you and admit the believing men and believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow, and that He may punish the hypocritical men and hypocritical women, by God’s granting to you, O Muhammad, what He has granted you of victory over the polytheists of Quraysh.” So they will be saddened by that and their hopes will be disappointed, which they had hoped to see in the people of faith in you of weakness and various forms of turning away from you in this worldly life, and burning in the Fire and remaining in it forever in the Hereafter. And the polytheistic men and polytheistic women, He says: And He will likewise punish the polytheistic men and polytheistic women who think of God that He will not grant you victory and the people of faith in you over your enemies, and that He will not make His word prevail and make it supreme over the word of the disbelievers in Him.

This was the evil of their suspicions that God mentioned in this place. God Almighty says: Upon the hypocrites, men and women, and the polytheists who suspected the circle of evil, meaning the circle of torment would revolve around them. The reciters differed in their recitation of this word. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as Da’irat al-Su’ with a fat-ha on the seen.

Some of the reciters of Basra read it as Da’irat al-Su’ with a damma on the seen. Al-Farra’ used to say: The fat-ha is more widespread in the seen. He said: The Arabs rarely say Da’irat al-Su’ with a damma on the seen. The fat-ha on the seen is more pleasing to me than the damma, because the Arabs say: He is a bad man with a fat-ha on the seen, but they do not say: He is a bad man. And His statement, And God’s wrath was upon them, means that God became angry with them and cursed them, meaning that He distanced them and removed them from His mercy. And prepared Hell for them, means that He prepared Hell for them, which they will burn in on the Day of Resurrection. And evil is the destination, means that Hell is evil as a home to which these hypocrites, men and women, and polytheists, men and women, will end up.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their recitation of this word.
The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as Da’irat al-Su’ with a fat-ha on the seen.
Some of the reciters of Basra read it as Da’irat al-Su’ with a damma on the seen.

x: And His statement,
h
And to God belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth
, God Almighty says:
h
And to God belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth

as helpers against His enemies. If He commands them to destroy them, they destroy them, and they hasten to do so out of obedience to Him. And God is Exalted in Might and Wise, God Almighty says: And God has always been Exalted in Might, and no one can overcome Him, and no one can prevent Him from doing what He wants, due to the greatness of His authority and power. He is Wise in His management of His creation.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Indeed, We have sent you, O Muhammad, as a witness over your nation regarding what they responded to in what you called them to, in what I sent you to them of the message, and as a bearer of good tidings” to them of Paradise if they responded to what you called them to of the upright religion, and as a warner to them of the punishment of God if they turn away from what you brought them from your Lord.
Then the reading differed in his statement,
h
That you may believe in God and His Messenger and honor him and respect him and glorify Him

. The majority of the readers of the regions, except for Abu Jaʿfar al-Madani and Abu ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAla’, read all of it with a ta’, li-ya-yi ... The correct thing to say about this is: They are two well-known readings with correct meanings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding his statement, Indeed, We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner, meaning: a witness to his nation that he has conveyed the message to them and a bringer of good tidings of Paradise for those who obey God, and a warner of the Fire. And his saying, And you honor him and respect him, the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation.

x: Some of them said: You honor him and respect him.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And they honor him means: reverence and they respect him means: glorify.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid informed us. He said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
And they honor him and respect him
, all of this is glorification and reverence.

x: Others said: The meaning of his saying and they honor him is and they support him, and the meaning is and they respect him and they magnify him.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qada:
m: And they support him means they support him and respect him. God commanded that he be made black and glorified.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement, and they support him, he said: They support him and honor him, meaning they glorify him.

c: Abu Hurairah Al-Dab’i told me: Harami told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Bishr Ja’far bin Abi Wahshiyyah, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: and they punish him. He said: They fight with him with the sword.

c: Yaqoub bin Ibrahim told me: Hisham told me on the authority of Abu Bishr on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: similarly.
b.via: Abu Bishr on the authority of Ikrimah

c: Ahmad bin Al-Walid told me: Uthman bin Omar told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Yahya and Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: similarly.

x: Who said that?

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd told us
m: regarding His statement,
h
And they honor him and respect him

, he said: Obedience is to God. These sayings are similar in meaning, although their wording differs. The meaning of ta'zir in this context is strengthening through support and assistance, and this can only be achieved through obedience, reverence, and veneration. We have explained the meaning of this with evidence previously, so there is no need to repeat it in this place. As for reverence: it is glorification, veneration and magnification. His statement,
h
And glorify Him in the morning and the evening
, means: And pray to Him, meaning to God in the mornings and evenings. The ha in His statement,
h
And glorify Him

, refers to the mention of God alone, not the Messenger. It has been mentioned that this is in some readings: And glorify God in the morning and the evening. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: And they glorify Him in the morning and the evening, in some of the recitations, And they glorify God in the morning and the evening.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thaur told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding some of the letters: And they glorify God morning and evening.

c: I was told on the authority of al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Mu’adh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
And they glorify Him morning and evening
, That you may believe in God and His Messenger, and support him and honor him,
h
and glorify Him
morning and evening. meaning: They glorify God. He returned to himself.

evidence.text: Then the reading differed in his statement, That you may believe in God and His Messenger and honor him and respect him and glorify Him.
The majority of the readers of the regions, except for Abu Jaʿfar al-Madani and Abu ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAla’, read all of it with a ta’, li-ya-yi ...

Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, And they glorify Him in the morning and the evening, in some of the recitations, And they glorify God in the morning and the evening.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Those of your companions who pledge allegiance to you at Al-Hudaibiyah, on the condition that they will not flee when meeting the enemy, nor turn their backs to them, are only pledging allegiance to God. He says: They are only pledging their allegiance to you to God, because God has guaranteed them Paradise through their companionship with Him in that regard. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
Those who pledge allegiance to you
, he said: On the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, “Indeed,
h
those who pledge allegiance to you

are only pledging allegiance to God. The hand of God is over their hands. So whoever breaks his pledge only breaks it to the detriment of his own soul.” They are those who pledged allegiance on the day of Hudaybiyyah. And in His saying,
h
The hand of God is above their hands
, there are two aspects of interpretation: One of them:
h
The hand of God is above their hands

at the time of the pledge of allegiance, because they were pledging allegiance to God by their pledge of allegiance to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the other: The power of God is above their power in supporting His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, because they only pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to support him against the enemy. And His statement,
h
But whoever breaks his pledge

, he only breaks it to the detriment of himself, God Almighty says: So whoever breaks his pledge to you, O Muhammad, and breaks it and does not support you against your enemies, and goes against what his Lord promised, he only breaks it to the detriment of himself, meaning: He only breaks his pledge because by doing that he is excluded from those to whom God promised Paradise for fulfilling the pledge. So his breaking of the pledge did not harm anyone but himself, and he only broke it to himself. As for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, God Almighty supported him against his enemies, whether the one who broke the pledge among them broke it or fulfilled his pledge. And His statement,
h
And whoever fulfills what he has pledged to God
, the verse, the Almighty says:
h
And whoever fulfills what he has pledged to God

of patience when meeting the enemy in the way of God, supporting His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, against his enemies, then He will give him a great reward, meaning: God will give him a great reward, and that is that He will admit him into Paradise as a reward for his fulfillment of what he pledged to God, and his trust in His Messenger to be patient with him during times of hardship, with the confirmation of faith. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention who told you: Bishr told us:

c: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: Then He will give him a great reward, meaning Paradise.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “O Muhammad, those whom God has left behind with their families, who did not accompany you and did not go out with you on your journey that you took, and the journey that you took to Mecca to perform Umrah, visiting the Sacred House of God, will say to you, if you return to them and rebuke them for staying behind you: We were distracted from going out with you by dealing with our money, and improving our livelihoods and our families, so ask forgiveness for us, our Lord, for staying behind you.” God Almighty says, refuting their statement: These Bedouins who stayed behind say with their tongues what is not in their hearts, and that is their asking the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to ask forgiveness for them. He says: They ask Him without repentance from them or regret for what they have done in their past of disobeying God in staying behind from the company of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the journey from him.

“Say: Then who can control for you anything from God?” God Almighty says to His Prophet: Say to these Bedouins who ask you to ask forgiveness for them for staying behind you: If I… I seek forgiveness for you, O people. Then God willed your destruction or the destruction of your wealth and your families, or He willed to benefit you by making your wealth flourish and your families better. So who is able to repel what God willed for you of good or evil? No one can defeat God, and no one can overcome Him. And His statement, Rather, God is All-Aware of what you do, means, the Most High says: “What is the matter with you, as these hypocrites among the Bedouins think, that God does not know what they are doing in terms of hypocrisy? Rather, God has always been All-Aware of what they do, good and evil. Nothing of the deeds of His creation, whether secret or public, is hidden from Him. He is recording them until He rewards them for them.”

And it was reported that when the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) wanted to go to Mecca in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah to perform Umrah, he mobilized the Arabs and the Bedouins around his city to go out with him, for fear that his people, the Quraysh, would expose him to war or prevent him from entering the House. He (blessings and peace of God be upon him) entered ihram for Umrah and brought sacrificial animals with him to show the people that he did not want to wage war. However, many of the Bedouins were reluctant to go with him and stayed behind. They are the ones whom God, the Most High, meant when He said, Those of the Bedouins who stayed behind will say to you, ‘Our wealth and our families have occupied us…’… And what we said about this was said by the people of knowledge of the biography of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his campaigns, including Ibn Ishaq.

m: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq on the same authority.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told us: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,

h
Those of the bedouins who stayed behind will say to you

, ‘Our wealth and our families have preoccupied us.’ He said: The bedouins of Medina: Juhayna and Muzayna. He followed them to go out to Mecca. They said: We will go with him to a people who came to him and killed his companions, so we can fight them. They made excuses for being preoccupied. The reciters differed in their reading of the phrase if He intended to harm you. The reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the reciters of Kufa, read it as dharana with a fatha on the letter dhad, meaning harm that is the opposite of benefit. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as dharana with a damma on the letter dhad, meaning misery and illness. The most amazing of the two readings is the opening of the letter Ḍād in this place, in his saying, Or He intended to benefit you. It is known that the opposite of benefit and harm is true, even if the other has a correct meaning.

x: God the Most High says to these hypocrites from among the Bedouins: And whoever does not believe, O bedouins, in God and His Messenger, from among you and from others, and does not believe in what he has been told, and acknowledges what he brought of the truth from his Lord, then We have prepared for them all a Blaze of Fire that will blaze against them in Hell when they enter it on the Day of Resurrection. It is said of this: I kindled the fire, if you lit it, so I kindle it with a blaze. It is also said: I stirred it, if you moved it. The one who kindles the fire is called a kindler because he stirs the fire with it. From this is their saying: He kindles war, meaning he who kindles it and incites it.
And His statement,
h
And to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth

, God Almighty says: And to God belongs the authority of the heavens and the earth, so no one, O hypocrites, will be able to prevent Him from what He intended to punish you for your hypocrisy if you persist in it, or to prevent Him from pardoning you if He pardons you, if you repent from your hypocrisy and disbelief. This is from God, the Most High, urging these Bedouins who stayed behind from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to repent and return to God’s command in obeying His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. He says to them: Hasten to repent for staying behind from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for God forgives those who repent. And God is Forgiving and Merciful, He says: And God has always been forgiving of the punishment of those of His servants who repent to Him for their sins and transgressions, and He is merciful to them by punishing them for their sins after they repent from them.

God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: “O Muhammad, those who stayed behind with their families and did not accompany you when you set out on your pilgrimage, intending to visit the Sacred House of God, will say: When you and your companions set out on your journey to what God has bestowed upon you and them of spoils, “to take them,” and that is what God had promised the people of Hudaybiyyah from the spoils of Khaybar, Leave us to follow you to Khaybar, so that we may witness with you the fighting of its people. They want to change the word of God. He says: They want to change the promise of God that He promised the people of Hudaybiyyah, and that is because God had given them the spoils of Khaybar, and He promised them that in exchange for the spoils of the people of Mecca if you left them in a peace treaty, and they did not take anything from them.
And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: He, meaning the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned from Mecca, and God promised him many spoils, so Khaybar was made his. Then those who stayed behind said, Leave us to follow you, wanting to change the word of God. They were the spoils to take, about which God, the Most High, said: When you set out to take spoils, and they were offered to fight a people of great strength.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thaur told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of a man from his companions, on the authority of Muqsim, who said:
m: When God promised them that He would conquer Khaybar for them, and God had promised it to those who had witnessed al-Hudaybiyyah, He did not give anything of it to anyone other than them. When the hypocrites knew that it was the spoils, they said, Leave us to follow you, wanting to change the words of God. He said, What He had promised them.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Those who stayed behind will say when you set out... The verse refers to those who stayed behind from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from Hudaybiyyah. It was mentioned to us that when the polytheists prevented the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from Hudaybiyyah, from the Sacred Mosque and the sacrificial animals, Al-Miqdad said: “O Prophet of God, by God, we do not say like the leaders of the Children of Israel when they said to their Prophet: ‘Go, you and your Lord, and fight. We are sitting right here.’ Rather, we say: ‘Go, you and your Lord, and fight. We are fighting with you.’ When the companions of the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) heard that, they pledged allegiance to what he had said. When the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw that, he made peace with the Quraysh, and most of them returned.”

x: Others said: Rather, what he meant by his saying, They want to change the words of God, is their desire to go out with the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his conquest. God Almighty said, Then say, ‘You will never go out with me, nor will you fight with me an enemy.’ (al-Tawbah 9:83).

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about the statement of God, Those who stayed behind will say, ‘When you set out to take the spoils, “Leave us, we will follow you… the verse, God, the Almighty, said to him when he returned from a raid, “And they asked your permission to go out. Say, ‘You will never go out.’ Say, ‘You will never go out with me, nor will you fight with me against an enemy.’” the verse. They wanted to change the words of God: they wanted to change the words of God that He said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to go out with him, but God, may He be exalted, refused that to them and to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is what Ibn Zayd said, a statement that has no basis, because the words of God Almighty And they asked your permission to go out, so say, You will never go out with me, nor will you fight with me an enemy were revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, upon his return from Tabuk, and He meant by it those who stayed behind when he headed to Tabuk to fight the Romans. There is no disagreement among the people of knowledge about the campaigns of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that Tabuk was after the conquest of Khaybar and was also considered the conquest of Mecca. This is report about those who stayed behind from traveling with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he set out on a pilgrimage, intending to perform the minor pilgrimage, and the polytheists who stayed behind from him in the Battle of Tabuk prevented him from going to the House. x: God Almighty says: God was pleased, O Muhammad, with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree. Meaning the pledge of allegiance of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the Messenger of God at Al-Hudaybiyah when they pledged allegiance to him to fight the Quraysh in the war, and not to flee or turn their backs to them under the tree. Their pledge of allegiance to him there, as mentioned, was under a tree. The reason for this pledge of allegiance is what was said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had sent Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him, with his message to the leaders of Quraysh, and Uthman was somewhat slow in responding to him, so he thought that he had been killed. So he called his companions to renew the pledge of allegiance to their war as I have described, so they pledged allegiance to him on that.

This pledge is called the Pledge of Ridwan, and those who pledged allegiance to him in this pledge were, according to what was mentioned by some of them: one thousand four hundred, and according to some of them: one thousand five hundred, and according to some of them: one thousand three hundred.
Mentioning the narration of what we described as the reason for this pledge:

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said:
m: “Some of the people of knowledge told me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Khurash ibn Umayyah al-Khuza’i and sent him to the Quraysh in Mecca, and carried him on his camel called al-Thalab, to convey to their leaders what he had come to him for. That was when he had arrived at al-Hudaybiyyah, and they hamstrung the Messenger of God’s camel, may God bless him and grant him peace, and wanted to kill him, but the Abyssinians prevented them and let him go until he came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” He said: Salamah narrated to us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said:

c: Someone I do not accuse told me, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: the freed slave of Ibn Abbas: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called upon Umar ibn al-Khattab to send him to Mecca to inform the nobles of what he had come for. He said: O Messenger of God, I fear for myself from the Quraysh, and there is no one in Mecca from the Banu Adi ibn Ka’b to protect me. The Quraysh know my hostility towards them and my harshness towards them, but I will direct you to a man who is more honored there than I am: Uthman ibn Affan. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called upon Uthman and sent him to Abu Sufyan and the nobles of the Quraysh to inform them that he had not come to fight, but had come to visit this House, respecting its sanctity. Uthman went out to Mecca, and Aban ibn Sa’id ibn al-As met him when he entered Mecca or before he entered it. He got down from his mount and carried him in front of him, then rode behind him and protected him until he delivered the message of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Uthman set out until he reached Abu Sufyan and the nobles of the Quraysh, and informed them of what he had come to say.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not send him with it. They said to Uthman when he had finished sending the message to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: If you wish to circumambulate the House, then circumambulate it. He said: I would not do that until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, circumambulates it. So the Quraysh considered it a reward for them, and the report of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Muslims reached him that Uthman had been killed. He said: Salamah narrated to us on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said:
