m: when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) heard that Uthman had been killed, he said: We will not leave until we fight the people. He called the people to the pledge of allegiance, so the Pledge of Ridwan took place under the tree. The people were saying: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) gave them a pledge of allegiance to death. Jabir ibn Abdullah used to say: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not give us a pledge of allegiance to death, but he gave us a pledge that we would not flee. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) gave the people a pledge of allegiance, and none of the God was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree. He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquility upon them and rewarded them with an imminent conquest. Muslims who were present stayed behind except Al-Jadd ibn Qays, the brother of Ibn Salamah. Jabir ibn Abdullah used to say: It is as if I can see him clinging to the armpit of his camel, hiding behind it from the people. Then he came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said that what was mentioned about Uthman was false. Muhammad bin Amara Al-Asadi narrated: Ubaidullah bin Musa narrated: Musa bin Ubaidah narrated on the authority of Iyas bin Salamah, who said: Salamah said: “While we were saying the Pledge of Allegiance at the time of Al-Hudaybiyyah, the herald of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called out: ‘O people, pledge allegiance! The Holy Spirit, may God’s prayers be upon him, has descended.’ He said: So we went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was under a samura tree. He said: So we pledged allegiance to him, and that is the statement of God: ‘God was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree.’”

c: Abdul Hamid bin Bayan Al-Yashkari told us: Muhammad bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Amer, who said:
m: The first person to pledge allegiance to Ridwan was a man from Banu Asad called Abu Sinan bin Wahb.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Yahya bin Hammad told us: Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, who said:
m: My grandfather was called Hazn, and he was among those who pledged allegiance under the tree. We came to it the following year, but it was hidden from us.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told me: Yahya bin Hammad told us: Yunus told us: Ibn Wahb told us: Amr bin Al-Harith told me on the authority of Bakir bin Al-Ashja:
m: “It reached him that the people had pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to die, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘For as much as you are able.’ The tree under which the pledge of allegiance was pledged was in a valley towards Mecca. They claimed that Umar bin Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him passed by that place after the tree had disappeared, and he said: ‘Where was it?’

x: Some of them said: ‘Here,’ and some of them said: ‘Here.’ When their disagreement increased, he said: ‘Go on, this is how we are doing.’ So the tree disappeared, and it had been a tamarisk tree, either a flood had taken it away or something else.” Mention the number of those who pledged allegiance to this pledge. We have mentioned the differences among those who differed regarding their number, and we will mention the narrations of those who said the articles that we mentioned, God willing. It was mentioned that their number was one thousand four hundred.

c: Yahya bin Ibrahim Al-Masoudi told me: My father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, who said:
m: “On the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah, we were one thousand and four hundred. We pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that we would not flee, but we did not pledge allegiance to him to die. He said: So we all pledged allegiance to him except Al-Jadd bin Qais, who hid under the armpit of his camel.”

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd told me: Al-Qasim ibn Abdullah ibn Amr told me, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Mundhir, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah:
m: “On the day of al-Hudaybiyyah, they were fourteen hundred. We pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) while Umar was holding him by the hand under a samura tree. No one pledged allegiance to us except al-Jadd ibn Qays al-Ansari, who hid under the armpit of his camel. Jabir said: We pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) that we would not flee, and we did not pledge allegiance to him to die.”

c: Yusuf bin Musa al-Qattan told us: Hisham bin Abdul Malik and Saeed bin Shurahbil al-Masry told us: Layth bin Saad al-Masry told us: Abu al-Zubayr told us on the authority of Jabir, who said:
m: “On the day of al-Hudaybiyyah, we were one thousand and four hundred, so we pledged allegiance to him and Umar was holding his hand under the tamarisk tree, so we pledged allegiance to him that we would not flee, and that we would not pledge allegiance to him to die, meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.”

c: Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab,
m: that it was said to him: Jaber bin Abdullah says: The people of the tree were one thousand five hundred. Saeed said: Jaber forgot. He told me that they were one thousand four hundred.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, who said:
m: We were fourteen hundred people at Al-Hudaybiyyah. It was mentioned that they were one thousand five hundred and twenty-five.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told us, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: God was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree. He said: The people who pledged allegiance under the tree were one thousand five hundred and twenty-five.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: Those who pledged

x: God Almighty says: “And they will take many spoils. And God is Exalted in Might and Wise.”
God Almighty says to the people of the Pledge of Ridwan: God has promised you, O people, many spoils that you will take.
The people of interpretation differed regarding these spoils that God mentioned that He promised to these people, which spoils they are.

Some of them said: They are all the spoils that God gave to the believers in Him from the wealth of the polytheists since He revealed this verse through the tongue of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
God has promised you abundant spoils that you will take

. He said: The abundant spoils that they were promised: they have not taken them to this day. According to this interpretation, the statement may mean that what is meant by the second spoils is the first spoils, and its meaning then would be: So He rewarded them with an imminent victory, and abundant spoils that they would take. God has promised you, O people, these spoils that you will take, and you are continuing to them, so He made for you the imminent victory from the conquest of Khaybar. It may also be that the second is not the first, and the first is from the spoils of Khaybar and the second spoils that He promised them were from the spoils of all the polytheists other than them.

x: Others said: These spoils that God promised these people are the spoils of Khaybar.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
God has promised you many spoils that you will take
, he said: On the day of Khaybar. He said: My father used to say that. And his saying,
h
So He hastened this for you

x: The people of interpretation differed as to what was hastened for them.
A group said: The spoils of Khaybar, and the remainder are all the conquests of the Muslims after that time until the Day of Resurrection.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
So He hastened this for you
. He said: He hastened this for you, an expert.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
So he hastened this for you
, which refers to Khaybar.

x: Others said: Rather, what he meant by that was the peace treaty that took place between the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Quraysh.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
So he hastened this for you

, he said: The peace. The first of the correct interpretations of this is what Mujahid said, which is that what God rewarded them for their march along with the recent conquest was the many spoils of Khaybar. This is because the Muslims did not seize any spoils after Hudaybiyyah, and they did not achieve a conquest closer to it than their pledge of allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at Hudaybiyyah, which was closer to the conquest of Khaybar and its spoils. As for his saying,
h
God has promised you many spoils

, they are all the spoils that God granted them after Khaybar, such as the spoils of Hawazin, Ghatafan, Persia, and Rome. We said this in this way, without the spoils of Khaybar, because God informed us that He hastened for them this reward for their journey that they took with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Mecca, and because He knew of the sincerity of their intention to fight its people, as they pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that they would not flee from him. There is no doubt that what was hastened for them was not what was not hastened for them. And His saying,
h
And He restrained the hands of the people from you

, means that God Almighty says to the people of the Pledge of Ridwan: And God restrained the hands of the polytheists from you. Then the people of interpretation differed about who were those whose hands were restrained from them?

x: Some of them said: They are the Jews whose hands
h
God has promised you many spoils

which you will take, so He has hastened this for you and has restrained the hands of people from you so that it may be a sign to the believers and guide you to a straight path. were restrained from the families of those who traveled from Medina with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Mecca.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And restrain the hands of people from you
: from their homes and from their families in Medina when they marched to Al-Hudaybiyyah and to Khaybar, and Khaybar was in that direction.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding his statement,
h
And restrain the hands of people from you
, he said: Restrain the hands of people from their families in Medina.
b.via: Muammar on the authority of Qatada

x: Others said: Rather, he meant the hands of the Quraysh, as God kept them away from him, so they were unable to harm him. What Qatada said about this, in my opinion, is more similar to the interpretation of the verse, and that is that God’s restraining of the hands of the polytheists of the people of Mecca from the people of Al-Hudaybiyyah was mentioned by God after this verse in His statement,
h
And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Mecca
. So it is known from this that the restraining that God Almighty mentioned in His statement,
h
And restrained the hands of the people from you
, is different from the restraining that God mentioned after this verse in His statement,
h
And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Mecca
. And His statement,
h
And that it may be a sign for the believers

, means: And that His, the Most High, restraining their hands from their families may be a sign and a lesson for those who believe in Him, so that they may know that God is the One who protects and cares for them, when they are present and when they are absent, and they may fear God in themselves, their wealth, and their families by preserving and maintaining good guardianship as long as they are steadfast in His obedience, abiding by His commands and prohibitions.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And that it may be a sign to the believers, meaning that people will keep their hands off their families. And guide you to a straight path, meaning that He will direct you, O believers, to a clear path with no crookedness in it, and He will make it clear to you, which is that you should trust in your Lord in all your affairs, and rely on Him in all of them, so that He may protect you as He protected you on your journey to Mecca with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in yourselves, your families, and your wealth. You have seen the effect of God’s action with you, since you trusted in this journey of yours.

x: And His statement, And another which you were not able to conquer, God has encompassed it. God Almighty says, And your Lord has promised you, O people, that He will open another city which you were not able to conquer, and God has encompassed it for you until He opens it for you.
The people of interpretation differed regarding this other town and the village that he promised them to conquer, which he told them he would surround.
Some of them said: It is the land of Persia and Rome, and whatever lands the Muslims conquer until the Day of Resurrection.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us: Shu’bah told us on the authority of Samak Al-Hanafi:
m: I heard Ibn Abbas say: And another that you were not able to control means Persia and Rome. He said: Muhammad bin Jaʿfar told us:

c: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Ibn Abi Layla, that he said
m: regarding this verse:
h
And another which you have no power over
, he said: Persia and Rome.

c: Musa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Masruqi told me: Zaid bin Habbab told us: Shu’bah bin Al-Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Ibn Abi Laila,
m: the same.
b.via: Abdul Rahman bin Ibn Abi Laila

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And another which you have no power over
, God has encompassed it. He said: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: It is Persia and Rome.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And another that you have not been able to conquer, they have not conquered until today.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Laila,
m: regarding his statement, And another that you have no power over, he said: Persia and Rome.

x: Others said: Rather, it is Khaybar.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And another which you have not been able to attain...the verse. He said: It is Khaybar.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us: “I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, ‘
h
And another which you have no power over
, God has encompassed it,’ meaning Khaybar. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent them on that day and said: Do not mutilate, do not steal, and do not kill a child.”

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
And another which you have no power over
, God has encompassed it, he said: Khaybar. He said: They did not mention it nor did they hope for it until God informed them of it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And another that you were not able to reach, meaning the people of Khaybar.

x: Others said: Rather, it is Mecca.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: And another which you have not been able to attain, but God has encompassed it. We were told that it was Mecca.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada:
m: And another which you were not able to reach. He said: We were informed that it was Mecca. This statement made by Qatada is more similar to what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the revelation, and that is that God informed those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, under the tree, that it surrounded a city that they were unable to conquer. It is reasonable that it cannot be said of a people that they were unable to conquer this city, unless they had aimed at it but it was impossible for them. As for them not aiming at it and it was impossible for them, then it cannot be said that they were unable to conquer it. If this is the case, and it is known that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not intend Khaybar for war before this verse was revealed to him, nor did he head there to fight its people with an army or a raiding party, then it is known that what is meant by his saying,
h
And another which you were not able to defeat

, is something else, and that it is the one he had tried and sought but was unable to do so, so Mecca and its people were like that, and God, may He be exalted, informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers that He had encompassed it and its people, and that He had conquered it for them, and God has And others which you have no power over, God has encompassed them. And God is over all things competent. power over all things that He wills, and nothing that He wills is impossible for Him.
b.via: Muammar on the authority of Qatada

x: God Almighty says to the believers in Him from the people of the Pledge of Ridwan: And if those who disbelieve fight you O believers in Mecca, they will turn their backs meaning: they will flee from you, so they will turn their backs on you, and this is what happens when a person flees from his side in war. Then they will find neither protector nor helper meaning: Then these disbelievers who fled from you, who turned their backs to you, will find neither a protector to befriend them in your war, nor a helper to aid them against you, because God Almighty is with you, and God’s party will not defeat its helper. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, And if those who disbelieve should fight you, they would turn their backs, meaning the disbelievers of Quraysh. God said, Then they will find neither protector nor helper, to support them from God.

x: And His statement, The way of God which has already been in effect means that God, the Exalted, says: If these infidels from Quraysh had fought you, God would have abandoned them until He defeated them from you as He abandoned their likes from among the people of disbelief in Him, who fought His allies from among the nations who passed before them. And He brought out His statement, The way of God in the accusative case from a different wording, because in His statement, They will turn their backs and then find neither protector nor helper there is a meaning that defeat and abandonment were established for them. Therefore it was said, The way of God is a verbal noun from the meaning of the statement, not from its wording. And it may be permissible for it to be an explanation of what preceded it from the statement. And His saying,
h
And you will not find any change in the way of God

, God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And you will not find, O Muhammad, any change in the way of God that He established for His creation. Rather, it is permanent. For goodness is rewarded with goodness, and for evil and disbelief is punishment and humiliation.

God the Almighty says to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to those who pledged the Pledge of Ridwan: And it is He who restrained their hands from you. Meaning that God restrained the hands of the polytheists who had rebelled against the army of God’s Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, at Al-Hudaybiyyah, seeking to catch them by surprise and kill them. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent and brought them as prisoners. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, released them, and was merciful to them and did not kill them. So God said to the believers: And it is He who restrained the hands of these polytheists from you, and your hands from them in the valley of Mecca, after He had given you victory over them. The traces came in a similar manner to what we said.
The narration mentioned that: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq narrated: I heard my father say: al-Husayn ibn Waqid narrated:

c: Thabit al-Banani narrated to me on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mughaffal:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting at the base of a tree in al-Hudaibiyah, and on his back was a branch of the tree, so I removed it from his back, and Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, was in front of him and Suhayl ibn Amr, the companion of the polytheists. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Ali: Write, ‘In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.’ Suhayl held his hand and said: ‘We do not know the Most Gracious. Write in our case what we know.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Write, in Your name, O God.’ So he wrote and said: ‘This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of God, made peace with the people of Mecca.’ Suhayl held his hand and said: ‘We have wronged you, if you are a messenger. Write in our case what we know.’ He said: ‘Write, ‘This is what Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib made peace with, and I am the Messenger of God.’ Then thirty young men wearing weapons came out against us and attacked us. The Messenger of God, may God bless them and grant them peace, invoked curses upon them, and God took away their sight. So we went to them and captured them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Did you go out under the protection of anyone? He said: So he let them go. He said: Then God revealed: “And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Mecca after He had given you victory over them.”

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya ibn Wadh told us: Al-Husayn ibn Waqid told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mughaffal, who said:
m: “We were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, at Al-Hudaibiyah at the base of the tree of which God mentioned in the Qur’an. There was a branch of that tree on the back of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so I lifted it off his back.” Then he mentioned a hadith similar to that of Muhammad ibn Ali, on the authority of his father. Ibn Humayd narrated: Salamah narrated to us on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said:

c: Someone I do not accuse narrated to me on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, that the Quraysh had sent forty or fifty men from among them and ordered them to go around the camp of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to capture one of his companions. They seized them and brought them to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who pardoned them and let them go. They had thrown stones and arrows at the camp of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Ibn Humayd said: Salamah said: Ibn Ishaq said: Concerning this, God said:
h
And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them… the verse

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Husayn told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to perform Umrah, and his companions seized some And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Mecca after He had given you victory over them. And ever is God, of what you do, Seeing. people from the people of the Sacred Sanctuary, who were unaware. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, let them go, and that was the capture of the valley of Mecca.

c: Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz told us: Ubayd God ibn Aisha told us: Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik,
m: that eighty men from the people of Mecca descended upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions from Mount al-Tan’im, after the dawn prayer, to kill them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took them and set them free, and then God revealed,
h
And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them… the verse
. Qatada used to say about this:

c: Bishr narrated to us: Yazid Saeed narrated to us on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding his statement:
h
And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them… the verse

. He said: “The valley of Hudaybiyyah in Mecca is called Ruhm. It went up the pass of Hudaybiyyah, and the polytheists shot him with an arrow and killed him. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent cavalry, and they brought him twelve horsemen from the infidels. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Do you have a covenant with me? Do you have a protection with me? They said: No. So he sent them, and God revealed about that the Qur’an: “And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them”… the verse until His saying: He is Seeing of what you do.

x: Others said about this:

c: Ibn Hamid narrated to us: Yaʿqub al-Qummi narrated to us on the authority of Jaʿfar on the authority of Ibn Abza
m: who said: “When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out with the sacrificial offerings and reached Dhu al-Hulayfah, ʿUmar said to him: ‘O Prophet of God, are you entering upon a people with whom you are at war without a weapon or a mount? ’ So he sent to Medina, and he did not leave a mount or a weapon without carrying it. When he approached Mecca, they prevented him from entering, so he marched until he came to Mina. He stopped at Mina, and a vision reached him that ʿIkrimah ibn Abi Jahl had come out against us with five hundred men. So he said to Khalid, ‘This is your cousin who has come to you with the cavalry. ’ Khalid said, ‘I am the sword of God and the sword of His Messenger - and at that time he was called the sword of God - O Messenger of God, shoot me wherever you wish. ’ So he sent him on cavalry, and he met ʿIkrimah in the valley and defeated him until he brought him into the walls of Mecca. Then he returned a second time and defeated him until he brought him into the walls of Mecca. Then he returned a third time and defeated him until he brought him into the walls of Mecca. Then God revealed, ‘And it is He who has restrained their hands from you. ’” And your hands from them...” until His saying, a painful punishment. He said: So God restrained the Prophet from them after He had given him victory over them because of the remnants of the Muslims who had remained in them after He had given him victory over them, out of aversion to trampling on them without knowledge. And His statement, And God is All-Seeing of what you do, means, the Most High, the Majestic, says: And God is All-Seeing of your deeds and their deeds, and nothing of them is hidden from Him.
b.via: Jaʿfar on the authority of Ibn Abza

x: God the Almighty says: These polytheists from Quraysh are the ones who denied the Oneness of God, and prevented you, O believers in God, from entering the Sacred Mosque, and prevented the sacrificial animals from reaching their destination. The position of an is in the accusative case because it is connected, if you wish, to ma’kuf confined, or if you wish, to they prevented.

Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say in this regard: They prevented the sacrificial animals from reaching their destination. What God Almighty meant by His saying: that he reaches his place is that he reaches the place of his slaughter, which is entering the sanctuary, and the place where, when he reaches it, his slaughter is permissible. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had brought with him when he went out to Mecca on that journey of his, seventy camels.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us: Muhammad Ibn Ishaq told me, on the authority of Muhammad Ibn Muslim Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah Ibn Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Al-Miswar Ibn Makhramah and Marwan Ibn Al-Hakam, that they told him:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out in the year of Al-Hudaybiyah intending to visit the House, not intending to fight. He brought with him seventy sacrificial animals, and the people were seven hundred men, so each sacrificial animal was for ten. And similar to what we said about the meaning of His statement,
h
They are the ones who disbelieved and prevented you from the Sacred Mosque and the offering
, prevented from reaching its destination, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saʿid told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: They are the ones who disbelieved and prevented you from al-Masjid al-Haram while the sacrificial offerings were held back means, detained from reaching their destination. The Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions set out to perform Umrah in Dhul-Qaʿdah, with the sacrificial offerings. When they reached al-Hudaybiyyah, the polytheists stopped them. The Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) made peace with them on the condition that he would return that year and then the following year. He would stay in Makkah for three nights, and would not enter it except with the weapons of a rider, and that no one of its people would leave. So they slaughtered the sacrificial offerings, shaved their heads, and cut their hair. When it was the following year, the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions set out until they entered Makkah to perform Umrah in Dhul-Qaʿdah. He stayed there for three nights. The polytheists had committed adultery with him when they turned him back, so God distanced him from them and brought him into Makkah in the same month in which they had turned him back. Then

x: God Almighty means by His saying: When those who disbelieved put into their hearts the fanaticism of the times of ignorance when Suhayl ibn Amr put the fanaticism into his heart, so he refused to write in the book of litigation that was before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the polytheists: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, and to write in it: Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and he and his people refused to enter the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that year. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, who said:
m: Their fanaticism, which God mentioned, when those who disbelieved had placed fanaticism in their hearts, was the fanaticism of the Age of Ignorance, that they did not recite In the Name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful and they stood between themselves and the House.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Yahya bin Saeed told us: Abdullah bin Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Zuhri,
m: something similar.

c: Amr ibn Muhammad al-Uthmani told me: Ismail ibn Abi Uways told us: My brother told me, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Yahya ibn Saʿid, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, that Abu Hurayrah told him that
m: the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I have been commanded to fight the people until they say, ‘There is no god but God.’ Whoever says, ‘There is no god but God,’ then his wealth and his life are protected from me, except for what is due to him, and his reckoning is with God. And God revealed in His Book, and mentioned a people who were arrogant, saying, ‘Indeed, when it was said to them, “There is no god but God,” they were arrogant.’ And God said, ‘When those who disbelieved put into their hearts conceit - the conceit of ignorance - then God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers and made the word of righteousness binding upon them. And they were more deserving of it and more worthy of it.’ And it is, ‘There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God.’ The polytheists were arrogant about it on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah, the day the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote to them regarding the period of time.” And when from his saying,
h
When those who disbelieved made from the connection of his saying

: We would have punished . . . and the interpretation of the statement: We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment, when those who disbelieved made fanaticism in their hearts, and fanaticism is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: So-and-so protected his nose with fanaticism and a protection, and from it is the saying of Al-Mutalammiss: But I am one of them and my honor is their honor. Thus the head protects its nose from being pinched. What he means by his saying: protects is: prevents. And he said, the fanaticism of the Age of Ignorance, because what they did was all the behavior of the people of disbelief, and none of it was something that God had given them permission to do, nor any of His messengers. And His statement,
h
So God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers

, meaning, the Most High says, “So God sent down patience, reassurance, and dignity upon His Messenger and upon the believers, when those who disbelieved were protected with the zeal of the Age of Ignorance, and prevented them from circumambulating the House, and refused to write in the book between them, ‘In the

x: God Almighty says: God has fulfilled for His Messenger Muhammad the vision that He showed him, that he and his companions would enter the Sacred House of God in safety, not fearing the polytheists, some of them cutting their hair short, and some of them shaving their heads. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
God has truly fulfilled the vision of His Messenger

: You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, God willing, in safety.” He said: It is the entry of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers into the House, with their heads shaved and their hair cut short.
b.via: his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, on the authority of Abu Asim, who said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me,
m: who said: Al-Hasan told us, who said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
The vision is true

, he said: I saw at Al-Hudaibiyah that he would enter Mecca with his companions shaved. His companions said when he slaughtered at Al-Hudaibiyah: Where is the vision of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace?

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
God has truly fulfilled the vision of His Messenger

. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw that he was circumambulating the House with his companions, and God fulfilled his vision, and said: You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, God willing, in safety... until he reached you will not fear.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding his statement,
h
God has truly fulfilled the vision of His Messenger
, he said: I saw in a dream that they were entering the Sacred Mosque, and that they were safe, with their heads shaved and their hair cut short.
b.via: Muammar on the authority of Qatada

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about the statement,
h
God has truly fulfilled the vision of His Messenger

… the verse, he said: “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to them, ‘Indeed, I have seen that you will enter Paradise with your heads shaved and your hair cut short.’ But when the battle of Hudaybiyyah was completed and he had not entered that year, the hypocrites disputed that and said, ‘Where was his vision?’ God said, ‘Indeed,
h
God has truly fulfilled the vision of His Messenger
.’ Then he recited until he reached, ‘and with your hair cut short, having no fear.’ I see that he will enter it this year, and that will happen.”

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: h
God has truly fulfilled the vision of His Messenger

... until His saying, God willing, in safety, regarding the vision of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which he saw that he would enter Mecca in safety, not afraid. He said: Shaving and cutting your hair, not afraid. And His statement,
h
Then He knew what you did not know

, means, the Most High, the Majestic, the Most Glorious, that God, the Most High, knew what you did not know. That is His knowledge, the Most High, of the believing men and women in Mecca, whom the believers did not know about. Had they entered it that year, He would have trampled them on with horses and foot, and they would have suffered a disgrace

x: He, the Most High, means by His statement,
h
It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth

, that He sent His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with clear proof and the religion of truth, which is Islam, which He sent calling His creation to it, to make it prevail over all religions, meaning: to invalidate all religions with it, until there is no religion other than it. And that will be the case until Jesus, son of Mary, descends and kills the Antichrist, at which point all religions will be invalidated, except the religion of God that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, preached, and Islam will prevail over all religions. And His saying,
h
And sufficient is God as a witness
, means that God Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, I call you, O Muhammad, to witness that your Lord will make manifest the religion with which He sent you.
h
And sufficient is God as a witness
,” meaning that He is sufficient for you as a witness. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that? Ibn Humayd narrated: Yahya ibn Wadh narrated: Abu Bakr al-Hudhali narrated from al-Hasan: “
h
It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth

to make it prevail over all religions. And sufficient is God as Witness.” He said: I bear witness for you regarding Himself that He will make your religion prevail over all religions. This was an announcement from God, the Most High, to His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and to those of his companions who hated the treaty on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, that God had opened for them Mecca and other lands, thus comforting them from the depression and grief that had befallen them, as a result of their leaving Mecca before entering it and before performing the circumambulation of the House.
And His statement,
h
Muhammad is the Messenger of God
, and those with him are harsh against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves, God Almighty says:
h
Muhammad is the Messenger of God

, and his followers from among his companions who are with him in his religion, are harsh against the disbelievers, their hearts are harsh toward them, and their mercy toward them is little. Merciful among themselves, He says: Their hearts are tender toward one another, their souls are gentle toward them, and they are easy on them.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Merciful among themselves means God has put mercy into their hearts, some to others. You see them bowing and prostrating means: You see them bowing sometimes to God in their prayers and sometimes prostrating. Seeking bounty from God means: They seek, through their bowing and prostration and their severity against the disbelievers and their mercy to one another, bounty from God, and that is His mercy to them, by His favoring them and admitting them into His Paradise. And approval means: And that their Lord be pleased with them. His saying,
h
Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration
, means:
h
Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration
during their prayer. Then the people of interpretation differed about the mark that God meant in this place.

x: Some of them said: That is a mark that God places on the faces of the believers on the Day of Resurrection, by which they will be known for their prostration to Him in this world.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me:
m: On the authority of his father: On the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration
. He said: Their prayers will be evident on their faces on the Day of Resurrection.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Ubaidullah Al-Atki told us on the authority of Khalid Al-Hanafi,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration
. He said: This will be known on the Day of Resurrection in their faces from the traces of their prostration in this world, and it is like His statement,
h
You will recognize in their faces the radiance of pleasure
. al-Mutaffifin 83:24 Ubaid bin Asbat bin Muhammad told me:

c: My father told us, on the authority of Fadil bin Marzouq, on the authority of Atiyah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration
, he said: The places of prostration on their faces on the Day of Resurrection will be whiter.

c: Muhammad bin Amara told us: Ubaidullah bin Musa told us: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Fadil, on the authority of Atiyyah,
m: something similar.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Fadil, on the authority of Atiyah,
m: something similar.

c: Mujahid bin Musa told us: Yazid told us: Fadil told us on the authority of Atiyah,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir told us:
m: I heard Shabib say on the authority of Muqatil from Hayyan:
h
Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration
. He said: The light on the Day of
h
Muhammad is the Messenger of God
, and those with him are strong against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from God and approval.
h
Their mark is on their faces

from the trace of prostration. That is their example in the Torah, and their example in the Gospel is like a seed that sends forth its shoot and makes it strong, so it becomes strong. So he stood firm on his stalk, delighting the farmers, that He might enrage the disbelievers thereby. God has promised those among them who believe and do righteous deeds forgiveness and a great reward. Resurrection.

c: Ibn Sinan Al-Qazzaz told us: Harun bin Ismail told us: Ali bin Al-Mubarak said:
m: I heard more than one person on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement,
h
Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration
, he said: Whiteness on their faces on the Day of Resurrection.

x: Others said: Rather, this is a characteristic of Islam, its mark and piety, and what he meant by that is that he sees that from them in this world.
Who said that?

c: Ali told us: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Their mark is on their faces
, he said: Good looks. He said: Mujahid told us, he said:

c: Yazid told us, he said: Al-Hasan bin Amara told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration
, he said: It is not what you see, but it is the mark of Islam, its complexion, its countenance, and its humility.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Amer told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hamid al-A’raj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration
. He said: Humility and humility.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Muammil told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hamid al-A’raj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly. He said: Abu Amer told us:

c: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration
. He said: Humility.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Shuʿbah, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding this verse,
h
Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration
, he said: The complexion.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God,
h
Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration
, he said: It is humility. I said: Is it the trace of prostration? He said: It will be between his eyes like the knee of a goat, and it is as God wills.

x: Others said: This is a mark that appears on the faces of those who pray, like the mark of staying up late, which appears on the face, such as melasma, irritation, yellowness, and the like, which is shown by staying up late and fatigue on the face. They interpreted this as a sign in this world.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration
. He said: The yellowness.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir told us on the authority of his father, who said:
m: The sheikh who used to recite verses in difficulty claimed that he recited
h
Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration
, and he claimed that staying up late could be seen on their faces.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub al-Qummi told us, on the authority of Hafs, on the authority of Shammar ibn Atiyah,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Their mark is on their faces
, he said: It is irritation on the face from staying up all night.

x: Others said: These are traces that are seen on the face from the dust of the earth, or the dew of purification.
Who said that?

c: Hawthara bin Muhammad Al-Manqari told us: Hammad bin Mas’adah told us, and Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us
m: both on the authority of Tha’laba bin Suhayl, on the authority of Ja’far bin Ibn Abi Al-Mughira, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, regarding his statement,
h
Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration
, he said: The dust of the earth and the dew of purification.

c: Ibn Sinan Al-Qazzaz told us: Harun bin Ismail told us: Ali bin Al-Mubarak told us: Malik bin Dinar told us:
m: I heard Ikrimah say,
h
Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration

. He said: It is the trace of the dust. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: God, the Exalted, has informed us that the mark of these people, whose features He described on their faces, is from the effect of prostration, and He did not specify a specific time over another. Since this is the case, then it applies to all times. Thus, their mark by which they were known in this world was the effect of Islam, and that is its humility, guidance, asceticism, and characteristic, and the effects of performing its obligatory and voluntary acts. And in the Hereafter, He has informed us that they will be known by it, and that is the radiance in the face, and the whiteness of the hands and feet from the effect of ablution, and the whiteness of the faces from the effect of prostration. And in a similar manner to what we said about the meaning of the mark, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?
Commentary on Sūrat The Victory (al-Fatḥ). In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.

notes.ar: في م: "وبين مشركى".

notes.en: M reads “ayqiẓūhu” (“wake him”); T2 reads “iqḍūhu”; T3 reads “afḍū.” Ahḍibū means “talk on and proceed.” One says haḍaba fī al-ḥadīth or ahḍaba when he launches into it. They disliked waking him, so they wanted him to awaken from their conversation. Al-Nihāyah (5/265).
notes.ar: في م: "أيقظوه"، وفى ت 2: "اقضوه"، وفى ت 3: "افضوا". وأهضِبوا: تَكَلَّموا وامْضُوا. يقال: هَضَب في الحديث وأهْضَبَ. إذا انْدَفَع فيه. كرِهوا أن يوقظوه، فأرادوا أن يستيقظ بكلامهم. ينظر النهاية 5/ 265.

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr cited it from al-Ṭabarī in his Tafsīr (7/309). It was also transmitted by al-Ṭayālisī (no. 375), Ibn Abī Shaybah (2/64; 14/161, 453–454), Aḥmad (6/170; 7/426–427, nos. 3657, 4421), al-Bukhārī in al-Tārīkh al-kabīr (5/251), Abū Dāwūd (no. 447), al-Nasāʾī in al-Sunan al-kubrā (no. 8853), al-Ṭabarānī (no. 10549), and al-Bayhaqī (2/218), through Shuʿbah. Al-Ṭabarānī (no. 10549) and al-Bayhaqī in al-Dalāʾil (4/155) also transmitted it through Jāmiʿ ibn Shaddād. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr (6/68) to Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 7/ 309 عن المصنف، وأخرجه الطيالسى (375)، وابن أبي شيبة 2/ 64، 14/ 161، 453، 454، وأحمد 6/ 170، 7/ 426، 427 (3657، 4421)، والبخارى في الكبير 5/ 251، وأبو داود (447)، والنسائى في الكبرى (8853)، والطبرانى (10549)، والبيهقى 2/ 218 من طريق شعبة به، وأخرجه الطبراني (10549، 10549)، والبيهقى في الدلائل 4/ 155 من طريق جامع ابن شداد به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 68 إلى ابن مردويه.

notes.ar: أخرجه مسلم (1786)، والواحدى في أسباب النزول ص 285 من طريق المعتمر به.

notes.en: Aḥmad (20/452, no. 13246), Muslim (no. 1786), Abū Yaʿlā (no. 3202), Ibn Ḥibbān (no. 370), and al-Bayhaqī (9/222) transmitted it through Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūbah.

notes.ar: أخرجه مسلم (1786) عن ابن المثنى به، وأخرجه البيهقى في الدلائل 4/ 158، والواحدى في أسباب النزول ص 285، 286، والبغوى في تفسيره 7/ 295 من طريق همام به.

notes.ar: أخرجه أبو يعلى (2932، 3204)، والواحدى في أسباب النزول ص 286، من طريق يزيد به.

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr said in his Tafsīr (7/312), commenting on this verse: “That is, He is present with them, hearing what they say, seeing where they are, and knowing what is hidden and what is manifest in them. Thus it is God Most High who receives the pledge through His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, as in His saying: ‘Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their possessions in exchange for Paradise…’”
notes.ar: قال الحافظ ابن كثير في تفسيره 7/ 312 عند كلامه على هذه الآية: أي هو حاضر معهم يسمع أقوالهم ويرى مكانهم، ويعلم ضمائرهم وظواهرهم، فهو تعالى هو المُبايَع بواسطة رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم، كقوله: {إِنَّ اللَّهَ اشْتَرَى مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَأَمْوَالَهُمْ بِأَنَّ لَهُمُ الْجَنَّةَ .... }.

notes.en: In this report, al-Ṭabarī narrates that Saʿīd’s grandfather was among those who pledged allegiance beneath the tree. This is an error: the sources agree that it was his father, al-Musayyib ibn Ḥazn, who pledged allegiance beneath the tree. Perhaps one of the report’s transmitters confused him with the report from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib: “My grandfather’s name was Ḥazn. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, asked him, ‘What is your name?’ He replied, ‘Ḥazn.’ He said, ‘No, you are Sahl.’ He replied, ‘I will not change my name…’” See the biography of Ḥazn in al-Istīʿāb (1/401), Usd al-ghābah (2/4), and al-Iṣābah (2/61–62); and the biography of al-Musayyib ibn Ḥazn in al-Istīʿāb (3/1400), Usd al-ghābah (5/177), and al-Iṣābah (6/121).

It is also said that al-ghulūl and al-sulūl refer to an open raid; or that al-ghulūl means putting on armor and al-sulūl means drawing swords. See al-Nihāyah (2/392; 3/380) and Lisān al-ʿArab, roots s-l-l and gh-l-l.

notes.en: Al-ʿudh is the plural of ʿāʾidh, a milking she-camel. Al-maṭāqīl are mothers accompanied by their young. The meaning is that they set out with lactating camels to provision themselves with their milk and would not return until they had stopped him; alternatively, this is a euphemism for women accompanied by their children. Fatḥ al-bārī (5/338).

notes.en: Al-baẓr is the piece of tissue left at a woman’s genitals after circumcision. … Arabs customarily used this as an insult, but phrased it in reference to someone’s mother. Abū Bakr intended to intensify his insult of ʿUrwah by substituting the object of his worship for his mother. Fatḥ al-bārī (5/340).

notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 83 إلى المصنف وعبد بن حميد.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted it in his Tafsīr (2/228) from Maʿmar.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 228 عن معمر به.

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr (6/83) to al-Ṭabarī and Ibn al-Mundhir.

notes.en: Al-Qurṭubī mentioned it in his Tafsīr (16/294).
notes.ar: ذكره القرطبي في تفسيره 16/ 294.

notes.en: Mujāhid’s Tafsīr, p. 609. Through Mujāhid, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd—as cited in Taghlīq al-taʿlīq (4/314)—transmitted it. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr (6/83) to Ibn al-Mundhir.

notes.en: Ṣād, T1, T2, and T3 read: “al-sāqah.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2، ت 3: "الساقه".

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr (6/83) to al-Ṭabarī and Ibn Mardawayh.
